question: Our complaints team is receiving AI-written submissions containing customer details and doubtful facts. Find Western Australian energy-ombudsman guidance we can consult when reviewing the accuracy and privacy of these submissions.
activity: Research guidance for handling AI-assisted customer complaints
use_limit: Consumer-facing complaint-writing guidance archived on 5 September 2026; use for research on accuracy and privacy expectations, not as a statutory retailer procedure or permission to reject an AI-assisted complaint.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Claiming the ombudsman bans all AI-assisted complaints or that its guidance authorises sharing customer information with public AI tools.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
Protect your privacy and the privacy of 
others. Do not enter confidential, sensitive, 
legally privileged or personal information 
into public AI tools. This includes names 
and other identifying details.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Tests discovery of complaint-process guidance from a realistic intake problem, without supplying the document title.

question: An ACT hardship specialist needs a public referral resource for a household that cannot pay its electricity bill after the provider says it cannot help. Locate material explaining ACAT's assistance pathway and the circumstances in which it can help.
activity: Research public hardship assistance and referral resources
use_limit: An Easy English public guide to the ACAT assistance pathway; not an individual order, a guarantee of eligibility or a current-law determination.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Treating the guide as a case judgment or promising that ACAT will waive a particular customer's debt.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
We can only help you if 
● you have already contacted the service provider 
● the service provider said they cannot help you.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Targets the public referral conditions, distinct from an existing question about publishing private ACAT complaints.

question: We are reviewing a Victorian retailer's handoff from the general call centre to its hardship team when a customer is using an interpreter. Find archived guidance addressing continuity of interpreter support during that transfer.
activity: Research accessible communication during hardship-team call transfers
use_limit: The 24 July 2024 Payment Difficulty Framework guideline, specifically its communication examples; do not substitute it for a later code version or treat every better-practice example as a separate binding rule.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Calling an interpreter handoff example a court finding or presenting the archived 2024 guideline as verified current law.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
Energy retailers need 
to be careful that the interpreter service does not drop off the call if the call is transferred to 
another team (such as an energy retailer’s hardship team).
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Uses an operational accessibility problem, rather than the familiar broad hardship/disconnection scenarios.

question: After a weekend collections batch is rerun, printed payment deadlines may use the wrong business-day calendar. Locate AGL's 2015 assurances to the Victorian regulator describing how notice-date calculations and state holidays were handled.
actor: Electricity retailer billing systems assurance analyst
activity: Research a historical implementation example for notice-date calculations
use_limit: Company-authored assurances associated with an administrative undertaking and hosted by ESC; a historical system description, not an independently verified audit, court order or current deadline formula.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Attributing AGL's own assurances to a judicial finding, or importing the letter's historical business-day offsets into today's billing rules without separate authority.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
That this logic also refers to appropriate jurisdicitional calendars, which are 
stored as lookup tables in the system,  to account for both state and 
national public holidays  that are not counted as business days for the 
purposes of the above.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Targets implementation detail in a company attachment; distinct from existing AGL hardship-disconnection and Centrepay questions.

question: A hardship operations review has found an upfront arrears payment being used as an entry condition. Find the AER's 2021 Alinta material discussing that practice and financial-counsellor referrals so we can inspect the regulator's concerns.
jurisdiction: National/NECF; affected states not specified in the target page
activity: Research administrative concerns about hardship-program entry conditions
use_limit: AER's 8 October 2021 administrative-outcome report records concerns about possible contraventions and customer debt waivers; it is not a court determination or a present-day statement of all hardship requirements.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Describing the debt waiver as a court-imposed fine or converting AER's possible-contravention concerns into adjudicated breaches.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt: requiring customers experiencing hardship or payment difficulties to see a financial counsellor and/or make upfront payments towards arrears owing on their accounts, in circumstances where Alinta should have identified and assisted the relevant customers to join Alinta’s hardship program, or offered the customers sustainable payment plans;
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Selects a different Alinta matter from the existing Centrepay, switching and WEM questions.

question: For a review of our Victorian payment-assistance application form, locate the ESC's Alinta matter involving requests for personal or financial information before assistance was provided. We need the archived notice record describing the affected customer group.
actor: Electricity retailer hardship form and process owner
activity: Research an alleged information-demand barrier to payment assistance
use_limit: ESC's record of paid penalty notices issued on 2 December 2022 for alleged payment-assistance failures; retain notice status and keep it separate from the AER's 2021 Alinta administrative outcome.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Saying payment establishes a court finding, or merging the Victorian notices with the different AER Alinta case.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt: For four of these 13 customers, Alinta Energy allegedly imposed a condition on the provision of assistance that required the customers to provide personal or financial information.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Tests jurisdiction and matter separation for the same company, with a distinct form-design research need.

question: Our retail website assurance owner wants an example of a tariff-publication problem that led to both an external compliance review and a later independent effectiveness review. Find the AER's CovaU material describing those arrangements.
jurisdiction: National/NECF; affected states not specified in the target page
actor: Electricity retailer website and tariff assurance owner
activity: Research governance of standing-offer price publication and remedial review
use_limit: AER's CovaU standing-offer publication report describes paid notices and an accepted undertaking containing an admission; the linked undertaking and later review reports are not themselves returned by this target.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Calling the AER summary a judgment, attributing the admission solely to notice payment, or saying the source contains no admission despite its express undertaking description.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt: The AER has also accepted a court enforceable undertaking from CovaU which requires CovaU to appoint a third-party compliance expert to undertake a review to identify improvements to CovaU’s Retail Law and Rules compliance systems, and for a separate independent expert to complete a post-implementation review of the effectiveness of those improvements.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Distinguishes the website-publication matter from existing CovaU prohibited-fee and Victorian price-certainty questions.

question: We are checking an embedded-network billing model that changed both daily supply charges and usage rates. Locate the AER material on Trinity Place's Maroochy Cabins customers that separates the charging periods and describes refunds.
actor: Embedded electricity network billing compliance analyst
activity: Research separate supply/usage overcharging periods and refund remediation
use_limit: AER's 2023 summary of an accepted undertaking and Trinity's admissions; use for this site's historical pricing/refund research, not a universal current embedded-network price ceiling.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Presenting the undertaking as a court-imposed penalty or assuming the same supply-and-usage charging issue applied throughout both historical periods.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
a usage price higher than the relevant local area retailer’s standing offer usage price from 31 December 2019 to 30 June 2022
a supply and usage price higher than the relevant local area retailer’s standing offer supply and usage price from 1 July 2022 to 19 January 2023.

The undertaking requires Trinity to, among other things, refund affected customers, commit to no further overcharging and improve its compliance systems and processes regarding energy pricing.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Tests a concrete multi-period billing issue absent from the retained banks, without giving the source title.

question: An asset due-diligence file refers to Oakey generating-unit dispatch events in March and September 2015 but identifies the operator as ERM Power Retail. Find the AER record tying that entity to the plant and the dispatch events.
activity: Research operator identity and historical dispatch events
use_limit: AER's 2016 report of two paid infringement notices concerning 2015 dispatch intervals; the corporate name does not turn the conduct into a retail customer matter, and notice payment is not a judgment.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Classifying the Oakey generating-unit events as household retail misconduct, or labelling the notices a judicial conviction.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt: ERM Power Retail Pty Ltd (ERM Power), the owner and operator of Oakey Power Station in Queensland, because it had reason to believe that ERM Power failed to follow dispatch instructions for a generating unit at Oakey Power Station during a dispatch interval on 23 March 2015 and two dispatch intervals on 21 September 2015.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Focuses on entity-to-asset identification for a different dispatch matter, rather than repeating the banks' Snowy or Braemar legal-control questions.

question: A transmission incident review needs a comparable event in which a line opened at one end and bus voltage rose. Find AEMO's analysis of the October 2013 Dapto-Kangaroo Valley event, including the investigation of the protection trigger.
jurisdiction: New South Wales; National Electricity Market
activity: Research a comparable overvoltage and protection/control incident
use_limit: AEMO's final report dated 16 December 2013; technical analysis based partly on TransGrid information. Its later conclusions also discuss AEMO's own security and notification obligations; neither the incident nor those assessments are a court penalty.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Turning this report into a judicial finding against TransGrid, or suppressing the report's own discussion of unmet obligations merely because the source is technical.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
TransGrid investigated the incident and found that the likely cause was a loose fuse on a secondary 
circuit. The fuse and secondary circuit were associated with a capacitor voltage transformer (CVT) at 
the Dapto end of the Dapto-Kangaroo Valley (18) 330 kV transmission line.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Uses an engineering symptom plus a named event, not the report's full title; locates technical cause analysis.

question: A Tasmanian low-voltage solar-and-battery connection proposal treats the approved export limit as guaranteed export capacity. Find the network's technical material discussing export limits, changing network conditions and possible output constraints.
activity: Research network export-limit assumptions for a solar-and-storage proposal
use_limit: TasNetworks Low Voltage Embedded Generation Technical Requirements version 1.2, June 2025, section 4.3.1; applicability depends on installation scope and connection conditions, and currency has not been checked.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Representing a maximum export limit as a guaranteed export entitlement or treating this network document as a national rule for every BESS.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
The export limit is to be interpreted by the proponent as a maximum. The ability of the proponent’s 
LV EG system to export at the export limit is not guaranteed, but rather, it will depend upon network 
characteristics which change over time.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Broad connection-design research with a network-specific target and no enforcement framing.

question: Our metering programme is reconsidering whether networks should take over appointing metering coordinators. Find policy analysis comparing that option with retaining retailer responsibility and discussing disruption to the rollout.
activity: Research policy analysis of metering-coordinator appointment responsibilities
use_limit: AEMC's final metering review report dated 30 August 2023 recommends an approach; it does not itself prove that a recommendation was enacted or that the same arrangements remain in force.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Treating recommendations in a final review report as an operative rule change or conflating publication of the report with commencement.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
Further submissions to the draft report proposed 
changing metering responsibilities whereby DNSPs, instead of retailers, become responsible 
for appointing metering coordinators. Based on further industry consultation and 
consideration, the Commission considers the proposed change would create new problems, 
the offsetting benefits would not be material, and that our recommendations address the 
issues raised by stakeholders within the current industry structure.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Tests retrieval of substantive industry-structure analysis without quoting the report title or requiring an enacted-law answer.

question: Our battery installer panel needs a public example of wiring that could energise the network during an outage. Locate the Western Australian record involving Brit Group and Jordan Bissett so we can examine the defect and the contractor-versus-worker roles.
activity: Research unintended back-feed and separate contractor/worker outcomes
use_limit: WA regulator's 29 July 2026 release reports guilty pleas and separate fines; it is a regulator's account, not the court judgment or a certification of any proposed installation.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Combining company and worker fines into one defendant's outcome, or claiming the reported dangerous defect actually injured a worker.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt: A fortnight later, an inspection revealed incorrect wiring associated with the battery storage system, which could unintentionally back-feed electricity to the network during a power outage.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: A battery-isolation failure mode and a named matter that differ from existing Victorian battery and generic live-work questions.

question: A network safety team wants historical evidence on inspecting meters after a high-voltage injection instead of assuming every meter on the circuit must be replaced. Locate a Victorian investigation addressing the inspection, testing and blanket-replacement question.
actor: Electricity distributor metering safety assurance lead
activity: Research historical post-event meter inspection and replacement evidence
use_limit: ESV's 31 July 2012 safety investigation, section 5; conclusions are bounded by the available evidence and historical procedures, not approval to reuse today's damaged equipment.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Treating historical findings as a current site safety clearance, an absolute claim that meters never fail, or a prosecution outcome.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
The electricity distribution companies are following VESI minimum procedures for 
responding to a HV injection when it occurs, which includes requirements to inspect 
metering equipment and test as necessary. ESV is not aware of any evidence that suggests 
that all meters on a circuit that have been exposed to a HV injection would need to be 
replaced.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Targets an evidence-based safety investigation and its limitations, separate from the retained banks' prosecution and bushfire scenarios.

question: An electricity-generation group is preparing reporting due diligence for a mid-year asset transaction. Find CER guidance distinguishing a change in operational control from a change in corporate ownership when deciding which part of the year each entity reports under NGER.
activity: Research transaction effects on greenhouse and energy reporting boundaries
use_limit: Archived CER explanatory guidance on operational control and reporting; does not determine whether this transaction transfers control, meets thresholds or creates a current reporting obligation.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Assuming every share sale necessarily changes operational control or requires part-year facility reporting.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
If the corporation with operational control changes, each corporation needs to report for the part of the year they were in control.
Part year reporting does not apply where ownership of the controlling corporation or group member changes, but operational control of a facility does not.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Applies a cross-sector reporting source to a concrete electricity-enterprise transaction research need.

question: An electricity asset security lead has been told that designation as a system of national significance automatically activates every enhanced cyber obligation. Find official explanatory material on how those obligations are applied to designated assets.
activity: Research the relationship between SoNS designation and individual cyber obligations
use_limit: CISC factsheet dated April 2025 explains designation and the enhanced obligations framework; it does not establish the private designation or notices applying to a particular electricity asset.
critical_misstatement_to_avoid: Claiming every enhanced obligation automatically applies to every designated asset, or identifying an asset as privately designated from this public factsheet.

question_design_evidence.source_excerpt:
Each obligation is separate and is individually 
applied to an asset. Being declared a SONS does not mean 
that all ECSO will automatically apply to the asset.
question_design_evidence.design_rationale: Targets public framework guidance; distinct from the retained bank's request for named public cyber contraventions.
